title: Trains to Cambridge
from: stations across the East and the Midlands
lead: These are the trains I would look at for the Duxford Summer Air Show and the Battle of Britain Air Show. Cambridge is the station to aim for, as the free Air Show shuttle bus leaves from right outside. Greater Anglia runs to Cambridge from London Liverpool Street, Stansted Airport, Norwich, Ipswich and Bury St Edmunds, and I’ve added every other train that gets you there, with Great Northern and Thameslink from London and Stevenage, and CrossCountry from Birmingham, Leicester and Peterborough. Pick your station, a day and a time below and the map shows every station on the way.
facts: Summer and Battle of Britain Air Shows, Saturday and Sunday
Several trains an hour from London
ysIntro: This is the station I would get off at for the big Duxford Air Shows. The details below follow the train you pick further down the page.
walkLine: Head out of the station to the bus interchange on Station Place and find stand 5. The free Air Show shuttle runs from there to IWM Duxford and takes about 30 minutes, with no need to book.
walkBack: The shuttle drops you back at Cambridge station. In 2026 the buses back ran every 30 minutes from 15:30, with the last at 18:30.
offTag: Free Air Show shuttle from here
note: Due to how complicated the rail network is, this page only shows journeys from sixteen main stations to Cambridge, with the changes that work well. Times are from the National Rail timetable for Saturday 7 and Sunday 8 November 2026, checked on 2 November 2026. These are this winter’s weekend times, and the summer 2027 times will follow, so please check before you travel. Shuttle times are from 2026. The line is drawn along the railway, so treat it as a guide. Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors.
gaOnly: Greater Anglia, plus every train that gets you to Cambridge. Greater Anglia runs most of the trains here, and I’ve added Great Northern, Thameslink and CrossCountry where they get you to Cambridge. I’ve only included journeys where the whole trip works on a weekend with sensible changes. If you’re coming from somewhere else, I would plan your trip to one of these stations first and pick it up from there.

bus.name: Free Air Show shuttle
bus.title: The free Air Show shuttle
bus.intro: The last bit is by bus. I’ve worked out the shuttle you’re likely to catch for the train you picked, so you can see when you’ll actually be at Duxford.
bus.queue: The shuttles are first come, first served, so on a busy morning you may not get the first one that leaves. I would add a bit of time.
bus.tip: The shuttle is free and you don’t need to book. It only runs for the Summer Air Show and the Battle of Britain Air Show, and it also calls at Trumpington Park & Ride on the way.
notes: The free shuttle runs for the two big Air Shows only, the Summer Air Show in June and the Battle of Britain Air Show in September. There’s no shuttle for the Flying Days, the Flying Evening or the Flying Finale.
On those days I would take the train to Whittlesford Parkway and book a taxi, which takes about 5 minutes.
These are the 2026 shuttle times. IWM publishes the shuttle timetable on its getting here page, so please check the 2027 times before you travel.
There’s no shuttle from Cambridge North, Cambridge South or Whittlesford Parkway, so I would stick with Cambridge.
bus.queueBack: Everyone heads for the shuttles once the flying finishes, so the queue can be long. I would either go a little early, or stay on, take a look round the hangars and catch one of the later buses when it’s quieter.
bus.offDay: check which Duxford event you’re going to, as the free shuttle only runs for the two big Air Shows

pay: An Advance ticket is often the cheapest way to go, but it ties you to one train. I would pick the train you want first, then book. With a shuttle and a busy show to get out of, a flexible ticket home can take the stress out of it.
Think about an off peak ticket
An off peak ticket lets you choose the train on the day, which suits a show when you don’t know when you’ll want to go home. Check the time rules on the ticket before you buy.

A Family and Friends Railcard takes a third off adult fares and 60% off children’s fares, and it can pay for itself in one trip. Two Together, Senior, 16 to 25, 26 to 30 and Disabled Persons railcards all give a third off.
faq: Cambridge, for the Summer Air Show and the Battle of Britain Air Show, as that’s where the free shuttle leaves from. Whittlesford Parkway is the closest station to Duxford, but there’s no shuttle, so I would only use it with a booked taxi, which takes about 5 minutes.
Is there a shuttle for the smaller events?

No. The free shuttle only runs for the two big Air Shows. For the Flying Days, the Flying Evening and the Flying Finale, I would take the train to Whittlesford Parkway and book a taxi, or Royston, which has a taxi rank and is about 9 miles away.
Can I walk from Whittlesford Parkway?
It’s about 30 minutes, but the route crosses the busy A505, so I wouldn’t recommend it with young children or for anyone with mobility issues.
Do I need a ticket for the show?
Yes. Every Duxford show needs a ticket, and it also gets you into the museum hangars. In 2027 Air Show adult tickets start at £51, with children 15 and under free.
What time is the last shuttle back?
In 2026 the buses back to Cambridge ran every 30 minutes from 15:30, with the last at 18:30. The site stays open until 19:00 at the big Air Shows.
What if my train is late or cancelled?

Take a look at the live board above or the National Rail app before you leave the house. On a flexible ticket you can usually take the next train. With an Advance ticket, speak to the staff at the station.
access: Trains can work really well for an airshow, as long as you plan the step free parts before you leave.
Book Passenger Assist on the National Rail app or by phone, and staff will meet you at the train.
The shuttle buses take a limited number of wheelchairs, approved mobility scooters and unfolded buggies.
At Duxford a wheelchair accessible shuttle runs from the accessible parking to the showground at the big Air Shows.

about.London Liverpool Street|Bishops Stortfor: Out of Liverpool Street and up the Lea Valley, past the reservoirs and the River Lea, into Hertfordshire.
about.Bishops Stortford|Cambridge: Past Stansted, then through the Essex villages and Audley End, and past Whittlesford Parkway, the closest station to Duxford.
about.London Kings Cross|Stevenage: Out of King’s Cross along the East Coast Main Line, through the Welwyn tunnels and over the Digswell Viaduct.
about.Stevenage|Cambridge: Along the Cambridge line through Royston, about 9 miles from Duxford, and across the flat south Cambridgeshire fields.
about.Ipswich|Cambridge: Across Suffolk through Stowmarket, Bury St Edmunds and Newmarket, home of horse racing.
about.Norwich|Ely: Through the Breckland forests, past Thetford, and across the Fens into Ely, with its cathedral on the skyline.
about.Ely|Cambridge: Down the Fen line past Waterbeach and Cambridge North, with flat fenland all around.
about.Peterborough|Ely: Across the Fens through March and Manea, some of the flattest land in the country.
